records.targetThesis: A hazardous rail quarry where warnings, cover, and movable carts make the safest line legible.

sourceGrounded.note: Obsidian was transported in Jomon exchange; this is not evidence for a Jomon mine.

records.fantasyInvention: The subterranean quarry, rail network, and cave-in guardian are fictional.

records.targetThesis: A living forest where growth opens, blocks, and bends routes around a visible objective.

sourceGrounded.note: Northern Jomon environments included broad-leaved forests with nut-bearing trees and settlement resource use.

records.fantasyInvention: Animated roots, charms, and the heartwood guardian are fictional.

records.targetThesis: A sea cave where light, current, anchors, and dry shelves make movement decisions explicit.

sourceGrounded.note: Jomon sites include inland bays, lakes, and rivers; fishing and shellfish gathering used specific water settings.

records.fantasyInvention: Sea caves, tide magic, eel tunnels, and Tidemaw are fictional.

records.targetThesis: A ceremonial remnant where collapsed links and ritual fixtures force deliberate route recovery.

sourceGrounded.note: The property includes settlements, burial areas, ritual and ceremonial sites, stone circles, and earthworks.

records.fantasyInvention: Ancient ruins, hostile regents, and magic wards are fictional.

records.targetThesis: A pressured industrial corridor where smoke, lifts, heat, and breach points trade speed for safety.

sourceGrounded.note: Jomon pottery was heat-treated for cooking and storage; this does not establish an industrial furnace landscape.

records.fantasyInvention: The furnace complex, mechanical lifts, and Kilnheart are fictional.

records.targetThesis: A drowned precinct where current direction, anchors, and floodgates make the route change in readable ways.

sourceGrounded.note: Jomon communities adapted to warming, cooling, and marine transgression/regression near bays, lakes, and rivers.

records.fantasyInvention: Flooded architecture, controllable floodgates, and the drowned regent are fictional.

records.targetThesis: A vertical escarpment where ledges, wind, and anchors make elevation and exposure the route puzzle.

sourceGrounded.note: The World Heritage property spans mountain and hill landforms as well as lowlands and water settings.

records.fantasyInvention: Cliff traversal systems, sky shrines, and Sky Warden are fictional.

records.targetThesis: A grave landscape where cairns, spirit paths, and sealed tombs distinguish respectful detours from dangerous shortcuts.

sourceGrounded.note: Jomon sites include graves, burial areas, ritual deposits, and ceremonial places; burial layouts changed over time.

records.fantasyInvention: Spirits, ancestor magic, and the Barrow King are fictional.

records.targetThesis: An exposed white expanse where mirrors, brine, shelter, and long sightlines make orientation and risk visible.

sourceGrounded.note: Jomon settlements selected tidal areas for brackish shellfish gathering; this is not evidence for salt-flat settlements.

records.fantasyInvention: Salt mirrors, mirages, caravan husks, and the Salt Sovereign are fictional.

records.targetThesis: A frozen reliquary where whiteout, ice, wards, and thaw points make visibility and timing the decisive choices.

sourceGrounded.note: UNESCO records adaptation to climate warming and cooling across the long Jomon sequence; it does not establish a frozen reliquary.

records.fantasyInvention: The frozen reliquary, ice magic, duel rites, and Reliquary Warden are fictional.
